subject: Rose Park Lane zoning change and map amendment
topic: (EXTERNAL) Westpointe Comments for Tuesday Public Hearing regarding Rose Park Lane zoning change and map amendment
comment: On March 2020 the Westpointe Council held a public meeting regarding this proposal. The attached letter was presented at that time taken updated in July 2020 with the intent that a series of meetings would be conducted with the applicant Council members HDRC and community members to address this property's use. The pandemic slowed this plan said. As a result the attached draft letter was never sent to the City. I plan to talk with Austin Everett tomorrow and plan to this formal this letter and send it on to the City. I will also be requesting a neighborhood meeting with the applicant. I also plan on reviewing the staff comments in preparation for this public hearing. I plan to attend the public hearing and am in the process of contacting people in the area to hopefully bring a contingency to the meeting. I believe the issues should have been done long before now but do they oppose CP11& SPACE ZONING. They are concerned that the indoor soccer stadium could be seen as a nuisance to neighbors and the existing and potential future parking problems need to be addressed and resolved BEFORE any further expansion/development is undertaken. The neighborhood has hoped this issue would have been resolved cooperatively during the intervening two years. This is our second chance opportunity to make sure it happens this time. We are looking for specific action steps with measurable goals that can be accomplished and measured to the satisfaction of the neighborhood prior to this public hearing. Dorothy Owen, [redacted-phone], PS: Sharon Portmann, our secretary, will be sending you a short survey evaluating this Night Out, probably by mail.

subject: Thank you
topic: Re: (EXTERNAL) SLC Arts Grant - Thank you!
comment: Dear Dan, I wanted to reach out and extend a heartfelt thank you for your support of the arts and culture in our sweet little city. I have only been working in salt lake for about 4 years, but as a touring artist, I am excited to call my practice to a new level. I have thought for a long time about making art as healing objects. Here is some interesting tension there for me. Feeling worthIt in asking and able to receive. I'd also like to move more towards activism instead of simply making an object for private (or semi private) viewing. Murals, to me, feel like connection tissue. They're by necessity rooted in community. They are also inherently activist. This opportunity is granting me both the funds I needed to begin building a portfolio of murals, to be able to paint more of them in the future. I found, in the process of painting, so much joy. There is a different energy in public art. It's not entirely mine, it's ours. There is so much as a giving up. It feel like the opposite of loneliness. I get to speak about this piece and what inspire me, what moves me, throughout the hours and hours of painting. There's not hiding from it as there is when I'm in the studio, working on oil painting, it's almost all at the level of mounds feels collective. If feels direct, in so west light. I have entered some images of projects I've done due to complete after this help so far. some of them are in partnership with other individuals, some in partnership with community centers and others. As an artist to gain to make Salt Lake an even richer, more connected, more collectively inspired place. With gentleness and joy in late summer, Cate Nelson

subject: Homelessness
topic: Camp near elementary school and school is going to start.
comment: The newly created passageway to Backman Elementary school is littered with drug infested homeless camps from 500 N, Jordan River Trail to 900 N, Redact Street to 1000 West. Our children have to walk through, view and interact unsafe today, trespass, alcohol containers, syringe caps, and such. I walk through this every day, Commute as well as Toin surveying camp areas. The increase is alarming to say the least as May so often. I implore that cleaning up these camps is not a safe solution, the camps have continued to grow.
